"El TOPO" is a miniature for the world of INFINITY (the game) that dates back to 2007, when Corvus Belli's Infinity was still young, there were no 3D printing (not even for production masters) and the forums were starting to be active with just a bunch of guys in the spanish community.

El Topo was first found in Carlos Bostria's comic strips about the game. Later in 2008 I modeled (classic modelling with green stuff) a version of the miniature which was produced in very small quantity.
Now, this is actually my second try on creating a miniature with ZBrush, and I'm happy with the results, so you can get it for free!

Enjoy having a chubby mercenary in your ranks!

This is a Curtiss-Wright J2 Fury from the game Crimson Skies. **This version is bigger than game pieces and has a little more detail, the idea is to print it to be used as desktop token just for Crimson Skies fans**

**Remember you can leave a tip for the zeppelin crew here: [Beer for the crew](https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/toposolitario)**

Creating Crimson Skies planes for 3D printing is something that no-one has done previously. And it is a shame as the planes are pretty iconic and after many years from it discreet publishing, FASA's Crimson Skies still has a lot of fans who play or are willing to play from time to time.

I started this for testing the VR modelling tool Gravity Sketch, and I found that work flow is so quick that a new plane can be created from zero in almost an hour. First I made the Fury (the one I like most), and the results for it and the Peacemaker were so good that I finally am willing to complete the full series (basic box plus the Balmoral).

In the end... I'll have a good bunch of pieces just to frankenbuild almost any flying perversion just by dragging and dropping! XD

It is not designed to be printer friendly, but it is coming out perfect with resin printers and pretty good in FDM (I suggest to print them vertically with supports growing from the tail).

*Honk if you're a Crimson Skies fan!!*
